idea: Week three, from the story bank: written from the source, then corrected by two independent editors before voicing.
description: Between 2012-13 and 2022-23 Madhya Pradesh's cropped area rose 30%, from 23.1 to 30.1 million hectares, while its farmland (net sown area) rose 3%, from 15.4 to 15.8 million. Crops per 100 hectares of farmland went from 151 to 190: a rise of 39.3 points against India's 16.8.

Cropping intensity is crop area as a share of net sown area, as reported by the states; some figures are estimates and 2023-24 is still provisional. Andhra Pradesh, Telangana, Jammu and Kashmir and Ladakh are blank on the map.
source: Ministry of Agriculture and Farmers' Welfare, Land Use Statistics at a Glance, as published in the RBI Handbook of Statistics on Indian States, Table 57: cropping intensity, per cent (area sown with crops, counting each crop, as a percentage of the net sown area). Area figures are Tables 53 (gross sown area) and 54 (net sown area). Figures are reported by the states to the Ministry (the table marks some as estimates). 2022-23 is the last year that is not provisional.

done: Every figure recomputed from the source by the writer and again by a numbers-and-rules editor, who also read the answer text or table notes; a viewer editor then reworked the hook, the closing question and any repeated line. Fixes applied before voicing: Map note now also names that Mizoram and Manipur start at exactly 100.0 in 2012-13 (series flat at 100.0 for years; Mizoram +42.6 is the map's top rise); tests added; Closing question 'Is your farmland sown twice?' did not fit a map of changes (Madhya Pradesh itself is 1.9); now 'Did your state sow farmland more often?' with matching voice; Title gained its period: 'Madhya Pradesh: Farmland Sown 1.5×, Then 1.9×, in 10 Years'; Hook: 'farmland sown 1.5 times ... 1.9 times' -> 'cropped area up 30%, farmland up 3%'; Fact card repeated the hook's percentages -> +7.0 million ha vs +0.5 million ha (two new tests)
The fourth card printed asterisks, and its bar figures ('7.0 million ha') wrapped onto three lines. The bars now show 7.0 and 0.5, with 'Bars in million hectares' in the line under them.
